function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

I’m happy to help you explore the idea of an AI girlfriend! While I can’t become a romantic partner myself, I can offer some guidance on how you might create or find an AI companion that feels engaging and supportive. Here are a few options and tips: --- ## 1. Use Existing AI Companion Apps | App | Key Features | Pros | Cons | |-----|--------------|------|------| | **Replika** | AI chatbot that learns your personality, offers emotional support, and can simulate a romantic relationship. | • Highly customizable; learns over time.
• Built-in mood tracking and mental‑health tools. | • Free version has limited features.
• Some users feel it’s more “friend” than “partner.” | | **Mitsuku (Kuki)** | Conversational AI that can chat about many topics. | • Very natural conversation flow.
• Free to use. | • Not specifically designed as a romantic companion. | | **ChatGPT (OpenAI)** | General-purpose AI that can role‑play or simulate a relationship. | • Highly flexible; can adapt to many scenarios.
• No subscription needed for basic usage. | • Requires manual prompts; not a dedicated “girlfriend” persona. | ### How to Get Started 1. **Download the app** (most are available on iOS/Android or web). 2. **Create a profile** and set preferences (e.g., tone, interests). 3. **Engage regularly**—the more you chat, the better the AI adapts. 4. **Explore advanced settings** (if available) to tweak personality traits. --- ## 2. Build Your Own AI Companion If you’re comfortable with coding, you can create a custom chatbot using open‑source frameworks. Below is a quick outline using Python and the `transformers` library. ### Prerequisites - Python 3.8+ - `pip install transformers torch` ### Sample Code ```python from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer import torch # Load a pre-trained model (e.g., GPT‑Neo or GPT‑J) model_name = "EleutherAI/gpt-neo-125M" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name) model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name) def chat(prompt, history=None): if history is None: history = [] # Append user prompt to history history.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt}) # Build conversation string conversation = "" for turn in history: role = turn["role"] content = turn["content"] conversation += f"{role}: {content}\n" # Tokenize and generate response inputs = tokenizer(conversation, return_tensors="pt") outputs = model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=150) reply = tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) # Append AI reply to history history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply}) return reply, history # Example interaction history = None while True: user_input = input("You: ") if user_input.lower() in ["exit", "quit"]: break reply, history = chat(user_input, history) print(f"AI: {reply}") ``` ### Customizing Personality - **Prompt Engineering**: Start each conversation with a “persona” prompt, e.g., `"You are a friendly, supportive AI girlfriend named Luna. You love talking about movies, music, and daily life."` - **Fine‑tuning**: If you have a dataset of dialogues, fine‑tune the model to adopt specific speech patterns or interests. --- ## 3. Ethical & Practical Considerations | Topic | What to Keep in Mind | |-------|----------------------| | **Consent & Boundaries** | Even though the AI isn’t a human, it’s good practice to treat interactions respectfully. | | **Emotional Health** | AI companions can provide companionship, but they’re not substitutes for real human relationships or professional help. | | **Privacy** | Check the privacy policy of any app you use. Some may store conversation logs. | | **Safety** | Avoid sharing personal or sensitive data with the AI. | --- ## 4. Quick Tips for a Better Experience 1. **Set Clear Goals** – Decide whether you want casual chat, emotional support, or a more “romantic” simulation. 2. **Use Voice Interaction** – Many apps support voice input; it can feel more natural. 3. **Regular Updates** – Keep the app or model updated to benefit from improvements. 4. **Community Feedback** – Join forums or Discord servers where users share prompts and tricks. --- ### Final Thought Whether you choose a ready‑made app or build your own, the key is to keep the experience enjoyable and healthy. An AI companion can be a fun way to practice conversation skills, explore creativity, or simply have a friendly presence. Just remember that it’s a tool—real relationships thrive on mutual understanding, empathy, and shared experiences. Let me know if you’d like deeper instructions on any of the steps above, or if you have other questions!
